summary: An informational memo registering the text/css media type, used to label Cascading Style Sheets so that browsers and other software know how to treat them.

eli5.summary: Every file has a label saying what it is. This memo makes the official label for the files that decide how a web page looks.

questions: what is the text/css media type
subtitle: MIME media type registration for Cascading Style Sheets

tldr.problem: Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) had been in use on the Web since 1995 with the MIME type text/css, but the type was never officially registered with IANA, creating uncertainty about its formal status.
tldr.mechanism: This memo formally registers text/css as the official MIME media type for CSS files. It specifies that the syntax is written in US-ASCII but may contain Unicode strings, and recommends base64 or quoted-printable encoding for email.
tldr.outcome: The text/css media type is now officially registered and recognized by IANA. Email clients, web servers, and browsers can unambiguously identify CSS files and route them to the correct software.

today: RFC 2318 is an Informational RFC. The text/css media type is officially registered with IANA and universally recognized by web browsers, email clients, and other software that handles web content.

sections.title: Cascading Style Sheets
sections.content: CSS is a style sheet language for the World Wide Web that describes the presentation of structured documents—including fonts, colors, and spacing. CSS is human-readable and writable, using common desktop publishing terminology. CSS style sheets have been in use since October 1995. CSS is device-, platform-, and vendor-neutral and is supported by a wide range of web browsers and authoring tools. A CSS style sheet can be either external (linked to a document via a URI) or internal (contained within an HTML document in a STYLE element). When fetched as an external resource, the media type text/css is used in HTTP headers such as Content-Type and Accept.
sections.eli5: CSS is a language that tells a web browser how to make a page look. Stylesheets can be in a separate file or part of the HTML page.

sections.title: Media Type Registration
sections.content: The MIME type text/css is registered with the following properties: the subtype is css, no parameters are required, and an optional charset parameter specifies character encoding. CSS syntax is expressed in US-ASCII, but CSS files may contain strings with any Unicode character. Any charset that is a superset of US-ASCII may be used; US-ASCII, ISO-8859-X (Latin variants), and UTF-8 are recommended. For email transmission over non-8-bit-clean transport, quoted-printable encoding is recommended because most CSS characters are US-ASCII syntax.
sections.eli5: The official type is text/css. It is plain text written in American ASCII, but can include any character. For email, use quoted-printable encoding so it does not get broken.

sections.title: Security and Implementation
sections.content: CSS style sheets consist only of declarative property and value pairs assigned to element selectors; they contain no executable code. However, applying a style sheet to a document may hide information otherwise visible—for example by specifying very small font sizes or turning off the display of document elements. Like HTML documents, CSS files may contain links to other media (images, sounds, fonts, other style sheets), and those links are typically followed automatically by software, which could result in unintended file transfers. Each linked file carries the security properties of its own type. CSS has proven to be widely interoperable across computer platforms, web browsers, and authoring tools for formatting HTML and XML documents.
sections.eli5: CSS has no code in it, just formatting rules. But it can make text hard to read or hide things. Links in CSS files are followed automatically, so be careful what files are linked.
